tracks.narration: Turn the voltage on a diode up from zero — when does current finally start to flow?
Put an adjustable source across a diode and measure the current. The diode is forward biased when V D is positive, anode to cathode.
Plot the current against the voltage. Below the knee — about zero point six volts for silicon — almost no current flows. Cross the knee and the current climbs nearly exponentially.
Sweep the source voltage and watch the operating point slide. Reverse bias — current pinned at zero. Past the knee — current rockets up.
For pencil-and-paper work, treat it as a switch: open below the knee, a tiny fixed drop above.
